title: Product Update: August 2025
summary: This month: Stronger security, smarter accruals, seamless ID checks, and custom attributes to tailor paperwork and reporting.
body_text: Welcome to this month's update of newly released features. In August we rolled out stronger security with MFA, smarter accruals tracking with dynamic dates, seamless ID verification in contractor onboarding, and custom attributes in onboarding. Plus, Google Wallet integration and compliance improvements to keep your teams moving fast and staying protected. Pay Accruals in Dashboard Easily view worker balances, rules, and policy activity in one place. Payroll admins can preview policies ahead of runs and manage accruals without waiting for checks to process. Dynamic Accrual Date Policies can now roll over based on any date, such as a worker’s anniversary date, instead of an annual cutoff. That means cleaner compliance, less manual adjustment, and a smoother worker experience. Paycards for Google Wallet ‍ Workers can now add Paycards to Google Wallet in just one tap for faster, contactless access to earnings. Platform Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) ‍ MFA is now live across Zeal. Workers log in with email + SMS verification; admins with email MFA. This adds an extra layer of protection to payroll and onboarding. Onboard Contractor Verification ‍ Contractors can now upload IDs and complete a selfie check during onboarding. Prevent fraud and keep workflows streamlined with the process embedded in a unified onboarding experience. ‍ Custom Attributes You can now use custom attributes in the dashboard and the API to capture custom data during onboarding. Use this to tailor paperwork for different worker groups, collect specific data like certifications, generate more detailed reports, or survey workers for feedback. ICYMI: Supplement B Recertification Supplement B updates are now easier to manage in the I-9 Hub. When work authorizations change—like an EAD card expiring or being revoked—admins can quickly ask workers to provide new documents that will recertify their eligibility. ‍ If you’re looking to upgrade your worker and admin experience, or optimize your workflows and your cash flows, please contact us . We’d love to show you how our solutions can help you reduce costs, improve worker retention, and unlock new revenue streams.

body_text: Press Releases 2026 Home Investors Press Releases SunCoke Energy, Inc. Announces Fourth Quarter 2025 Earnings Date LISLE, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- SunCoke Energy, Inc. (NYSE: SXC) plans to release its fourth quarter 2025 financial results and 2026 guidance on Tuesday, February 17, 2026, before trading opens on the New York Stock Exchange. SXC will host its quarterly earnings call at 11:00 am ET on February 17, 2026. The conference call will be webcast live at https://event.choruscall.com/mediaframe/webcast.html?webcastid=6AQEfKx3 and archived for replay in the Investors section of www.suncoke.com . Investors and analysts may participate in this call by dialing 1-833-821-7847 in the U.S. or 1-412-652-1261 if outside the U.S., and asking to be joined into the SunCoke Energy, Inc. call. ABOUT SUNCOKE ENERGY, INC. SunCoke Energy, Inc. (NYSE: SXC) supplies high-quality coke to domestic and international customers. Our coke is used in the blast furnace production of steel as well as the foundry production of casted iron, with the majority of sales under long-term, take-or-pay contracts. We also export coke to overseas customers seeking high-quality product for their blast furnaces. Our process utilizes an innovative heat-recovery technology that captures excess heat for steam or electrical power generation and draws upon more than 60 years of cokemaking experience to operate our facilities in Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Virginia and Brazil. Our industrial services business provides export and domestic material handling services to coke, coal, steel, power and other bulk customers, as well as mission-critical services to leading steel producers globally. The logistics terminals have the collective capacity to mix and transload more than 40 million tons of material each year and are strategically located to reach Gulf Coast, East Coast, Great Lakes and international ports. Additional industrial services include the removal, handling, and processing of molten slag at customer sites, as well as preparation and transportation of metal scraps, raw materials, and finished products. To learn more about SunCoke Energy, Inc., visit our website at www.suncoke.com . title: SABINE ROYALTY TRUST ANNOUNCES MONTHLY CASH DISTRIBUTION FOR JULY 2026
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Argent Trust Company, as Trustee of the Sabine Royalty Trust (NYSE: SBR), today declared a cash distribution to the holders of its units of...
body_text: DALLAS , July 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Argent Trust Company, as Trustee of the Sabine Royalty Trust (NYSE: SBR ), today declared a cash distribution to the holders of its units of beneficial interest of $0.429150 per unit, payable on July 29, 2026, to unit holders of record on July 15, 2026. Sabine's cash distribution history, current and prior year financial reports and tax information booklets, a link to filings made with the Securities and Exchange Commission and more can be found on its website at http://www.sbr-sabine.com/ . Additionally, printed reports can be requested and are mailed free of charge. This distribution reflects primarily the oil production for April 2026 and the gas production for March 2026, which is considered current production. Preliminary production volumes are approximately 54,139 barrels of oil and 1,074,976 Mcf of gas. Preliminary prices are approximately $87.11 per barrel of oil and $2.41 per Mcf of gas. This month's distribution is lower than the previous month's primarily due to a decrease in natural gas pricing, slightly offset by higher oil and natural gas production, along with higher oil pricing. The table below compares this month's production and prices to the previous month's: Net to Trust Sales Volumes (a) Average Price (a) Oil (bbls) Gas (Mcf) Oil (per bbl) Gas (per Mcf) Current Month 54,139 1,074,976 $87.11 $2.41 Prior Month 50,742 896,486 $80.78 $4.70 (a)Sales volumes are recorded in the month the Trust receives and identifies the related royalty income. Because of this, sales volumes and pricing may fluctuate from month to month based on the timing of cash receipts. Revenues are only distributed after they are received, verified, and posted. Most energy companies normally issue payment of royalties on or about the 25th of every month, and depending on mail delivery, a varying amount of royalties are not received until after the revenue posting on the last business day of the month. The revenues received after that date will be posted within 30 days of receipt. Due to the timing of the end of the month of June, approximately $1,029,000 of revenue received will be posted in the following month of July in addition to normal cash receipts received during July. Since the close of business in June and prior to this press release, approximately $1,462,000 in revenue has been received. The 2025 Annual Report with Form 10-K and the December 31, 2025, Reserve Summary are available on the Sabine website at http://www.sbr-sabine.com/ . summary: Compare medical record retrieval software for small personal injury law firms and see why Codes Health stands out with complete records in a couple of weeks, AI powered analysis, and flat fee pricing.
body_text: Small personal injury law firms face a familiar frustration: medical record retrieval that drags on for weeks or months while providers, authorizations, and follow-up calls pile up. Some Texas physician requests are subject to a 15-business-day deadline once the physician receives valid consent and any required payment, but actual retrieval timelines vary widely by provider type, request method, authorization quality, and applicable state law. For practices without dedicated paralegal teams, this bottleneck directly affects cash flow, settlement timelines, and case capacity. This guide evaluates 12 solutions for small PI firms, with Codes Health emerging as the top choice for firms prioritizing completeness, AI-powered analysis, and verified accuracy. Key Takeaways Medical record retrieval timelines vary widely by provider, request method, and state law, and can stretch well beyond the deadlines that apply to some individual request types Incomplete or defective authorizations are a common cause of rejected or delayed requests, and AI-powered platforms can help catch these errors before submission Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks, not months, with AI-human hybrid verification purpose-built for personal injury workflows Integration with case management software like Filevine cuts down on context switching and keeps a single operational record for each matter Security certifications range from baseline HIPAA compliance to premium SOC 2 Type II certification Flat-fee pricing models can provide cost predictability that matters for contingency-fee practices Understanding the Unique Medical Record Needs of Small Personal Injury Law Firms Small PI firms often function as their own pre-litigation department, handling case qualification, damages documentation, demand preparation, and negotiation without the staff resources of larger practices. This creates distinct medical record needs: Volume challenges : A solo practitioner managing 20 active cases with several providers each can easily face well over 100 record requests a year. Without automation, this consumes substantial administrative time. Timeline pressure : Settlement negotiations and statutes of limitations create hard deadlines. Extended retrieval windows compress case development timelines. Budget constraints : Per-page pricing models can generate surprise invoices. Small firms need predictable costs to maintain profitability on contingency cases. Quality requirements : Incomplete records can weaken negotiating positions and create trial surprises. Missing treatment notes, imaging studies, or billing records can undermine case value. The ideal retrieval partner for small firms combines speed, completeness verification, transparent pricing, and minimal administrative burden. These criteria separate modern AI platforms from traditional manual services. Evaluating Top Medical Record Retrieval Companies for Efficiency and Accuracy AI-Powered Platforms 1. Codes Health (Top Pick) Codes Health combines AI-powered analysis with human verification, purpose-built for legal workflows. Best For : Firms wanting completeness verification plus case insights, not just document delivery Turnaround : A couple of weeks, not months Pricing : Flat fee per case Security : HIPAA compliant Key Features : AI-powered chronologies organized by visit, with breach-of-care flagging for attorney review Missing Record Review cross-references patient history to identify gaps Proactive error prevention that catches authorization deficiencies before submission Multiple retrieval pathways, including claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, fax, and patient portals, to support completeness Custom CRM and medical software integrations for high-volume customers Why It Leads : Codes Health goes beyond retrieval to extract diagnoses, flag potential breaches of care, surface documented future expenses, and identify other case-relevant facts, with AI insights supported by human medical and legal review. Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, ensuring the platform constantly evolves, improves, and becomes more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices. 2. Tavrn An end-to-end platform extending beyond retrieval into case preparation. Best For : Firms wanting demand letter automation alongside retrieval Turnaround : Chronologies reported in under 24 hours for some services; contact Tavrn for current retrieval timelines Pricing : Published plans start at $299.99 per month for 20 retrieval requests Security : SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 certified Key Features : Hyperlinked medical chronologies AI demand letter drafting Integrations with Filevine, Litify, and Clio 3. LlamaLab Focuses on provider discovery and clinical case qualification. Best For : Mass tort practices needing qualification at scale Turnaround : Same-day to 48-hour retrieval, per LlamaLab, for qualifying requests Pricing : Retrieval charges marketed as case-specific expenses that may be recoverable, subject to applicable agreements Security : SOC 2 Type II, bank-level encryption Key Features : Reverse provider discovery that LlamaLab says identifies approximately three times as many providers as clients initially recall Licensed clinical team for case qualification Same-day to 48-hour retrieval advertised for qualifying requests Note: Rapid digital retrieval may cover only the records available through supported electronic sources, so firms should confirm that every requested provider, date range, and record type is actually included before assuming a request is complete. Codes Health says services promising same-day retrieval can leave gaps that require additional client involvement to resolve, which it says can contribute to client churn, and instead prioritizes working toward complete records in a couple of weeks. Hybrid Service + Technology Platforms 4. ChartRequest CaseBinder Combines automated workflows with a human service layer. Best For : Firms new to outsourcing wanting guided support Turnaround : Approximately 14 days, per ChartRequest Network : More than 12,000 healthcare organizations Security : SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliant Rating : 4.9/5 advertised customer rating 5. Records on Time (Rob Levine Legal Solutions) Built by a practicing PI attorney who experienced retrieval frustrations firsthand. Best For : Firms wanting attorney-built workflows with no contracts Turnaround : Rapid access reported for some electronic requests; timelines vary by provider Security : SOC 2 certified, HIPAA compliant Key Features : Reduced provider fees for qualifying electronic retrievals Integrations with Neos, Needles, SmartAdvocate, Litify, Filevine, Clio, CasePeer No contracts required 6. YoCierge Emphasizes integration breadth and budget control. Best For : Firms needing extensive case management integrations Turnaround : Same-day transmission of outgoing orders received before 4 p.m.; same-day upload of returned documents Security : SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 22301, CARIN accreditation, HIPAA compliant Key Features : Full control over custodial charges with a maximum amount setting Integrations with SmartAdvocate, Smokeball, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Dropbox A large and growing facility directory, current counts available directly from YoCierge Budget-Conscious Solutions 7. Record Retrieval Solutions (RRS) Publishes a clear per-request pricing structure. Best For : Solo practitioners and small firms needing predictable costs Turnaround : Approximately 16 days average, as reported by RRS Pricing : Contact RRS for current request pricing and to confirm whether summarization or chronology services are included Founded : 2014, by a professional with records industry experience dating to 1989 Key Features : Dedicated account management for high-volume practices 8. National Record Retrieval Strong case management integration with a security focus. Best For : Firms prioritizing case management system integration Turnaround : Reports an average 10-business-day turnaround for its record-review service; a current average for retrieval itself was not confirmed Pricing : Flat fee, without hidden charges Security : SOC 2, 256-bit encryption Key Features : Automated follow-up combining autofax, email, and live call center outreach Integrations with SmartAdvocate, Law Ruler, Filevine, Litify, Casepacer Company-published testimonial reporting more than 75,000 record requests across more than 25 litigations Enterprise-Scale Solutions 9. American Retrieval Company Established incumbent with electronic provider access. Best For : Firms needing Datavant connectivity reaching approximately 55 percent of U.S. providers Turnaround : Approximately 15 days, as reported by American Retrieval Founded : 1993; now part of U.S. Legal Support following a January 2025 acquisition Key Features : OCR-processed searchable PDFs Real-time tracking Long-term in-portal storage 10. Lexitas Full-service litigation support with records retrieval. Best For : Firms wanting vendor consolidation across court reporting, depositions, and expert coordination Founded : 1987 Security : SOC 2 Type II Key Features : Record Insights, an AI-enabled medical chronology add-on; contact Lexitas for current pricing and performance figures Legal nurse consultants available as a separate service Standardized nationwide rate model 11. Ontellus Enterprise-level security and compliance. Best For : Firms requiring strong security certification Turnaround : Most requests take fewer than 30 business days, per Ontellus Security : SOC 2 Type II certified 12. Compex Legal Services Longest track record in the industry. Best For : Risk-averse firms prioritizing stability Experience : More than 50 years Coverage : All 50 states Key Features : Asabell, an AI-powered medical record summarization product The Role of AI in Automating Medical Record Summarization and Chronologies AI-Powered Case Chronologies: Streamlining Review Manually reviewing a large medical file can require substantial attorney or paralegal time. AI-powered chronologies aim to compress that work by: Organizing patient encounters by visit across all providers Linking treatment dates to billing records automatically Flagging gaps in treatment documentation Creating hyperlinked summaries with source document references Codes Health's platform generates chronologies that group records by visit, exposing gaps that might call for supplemental requests before hours are spent on manual sorting. Insights Extraction: Identifying Key Information Beyond organization, AI extracts structured case intelligence: Diagnoses : Surfaces documented conditions, including those buried in dense records Breaches of care : Flags potential negligence indicators for medical malpractice crossover Future expenses : Identifies documented treatment recommendations supporting life care plans Pre-existing conditions : Highlights medical history that may require strategic positioning General AI platforms like ChatGPT are not reliable for litigation-grade medical record analysis. Codes Health's legal-grade AI is trained specifically for personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice workflows, combining automated extraction with human verification for higher precision. Leveraging Legal Case Management Software for Seamless Medical Record Integration Context switching between case management platforms, retrieval vendor portals, email, and downloaded file folders creates inefficiency and error risk. Embedded retrieval workflows within existing systems are the fix. The Filevine and Codes Health Integration On July 13, 2026, Filevine announced a partnership with Codes Health that embeds medical record retrieval directly into the Filevine case-management environment. This goes beyond a standard third-party integration. What Filevine users can do : Submit requests through Filevine from the relevant case file Track status updates in real time Communicate with the Codes Health team without leaving the project Receive completed medical records and billing inside the Filevine project AI-native workflow benefits : Validates authorization details, date ranges, and provider-specific requirements before submission Manages follow-up through calls, faxes, emails, and portals Checks completeness against the original request before delivery Filevine's CEO described medical record retrieval as a long-standing customer pain point that Filevine customers had been asking the company to solve for years. Why Timely Medical Record Retrieval Matters for Personal Injury Firms The Speed-Settlement Connection Delays can compound across your entire case pipeline: Case qualification stalls : Hard to assess case value without complete treatment documentation Expert review delays : Medical experts need records before providing opinions Negotiation weakness : Incomplete records can signal unprepared counsel to adjusters Statute pressure : Limitations periods leave little margin for lengthy retrieval windows Turnaround varies considerably by provider, authorization quality, source connectivity, and request complexity, so it's worth confirming a vendor's typical timelines directly rather than relying on a single industry-wide benchmark. Cost of Delay For a typical PI firm managing an active caseload: Staff time : Meaningful hours spent weekly tracking requests and making follow-up calls Opportunity cost : Delayed settlements mean delayed fee revenue Client attrition : Frustrated clients may seek other counsel during extended waits Malpractice exposure : Missed deadlines tied to retrieval delays can create liability Navigating HIPAA Compliance and Data Security in Medical Record Software Baseline vs. Premium Security HIPAA compliance represents the minimum legal requirement for handling protected health information. Any platform handling this data should use safeguards appropriate to its role and document its practices clearly, since specific obligations vary by entity and relationship. SOC 2 Type II certification represents a common premium standard: independent auditing of security controls over time. Vendors referenced above with this certification include Tavrn, LlamaLab, Lexitas, and Ontellus. Additional certifications some vendors maintain: ISO 27001 (information security management) ISO 22301 (business continuity) CARIN Code of Conduct Accreditation Data Access Pathways Modern platforms connect through multiple channels: Claims clearinghouses : Broader data access across participating networks Custodian integrations : Direct connections with participating record custodians Proprietary provider networks : Connections built and maintained by the platform itself Provider portals : Facility-specific access points Traditional channels : Fax, email, and telephone for providers without electronic access Codes Health connects through these pathways, aiming for broad coverage regardless of how individual providers manage their records. Choosing the Right Record Retrieval Partner: Beyond Just Documents Proactive Error Prevention Incomplete or defective authorizations are a common cause of rejected or delayed requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records, such as mental health, substance abuse, or HIV and AIDS related records, can force a resubmission and add real time to your retrieval. Other common rejection triggers include: Misspellings in patient or provider names Missing dates of service Incorrect or expired authorization forms Improperly formatted requests Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections. Verified Completeness Receiving documents doesn't guarantee receiving complete documents. Effective partners: Compare delivered records against original requests Identify missing facilities, date ranges, or record types Work with providers to resolve gaps before closing the request Document gaps for cases where complete records don't exist Visibility and Control Small firms cannot afford black-box vendors where requests disappear for weeks without updates. Essential transparency features: Real-time status tracking for every request Documentation of outreach attempts across calls, faxes, and emails Provider response history Alert notifications for issues requiring intervention Ready to Transform Your Medical Records Process? Long retrieval bottlenecks don't have to stall your settlements or consume your staff's time. Codes Health works toward complete medical records in a couple of weeks with AI-powered analysis, human verification, and proactive error prevention, purpose-built for personal injury workflows. How can small personal injury firms ensure HIPAA compliance when handling medical records? Partner with retrieval vendors that maintain HIPAA compliance at minimum, and preferably SOC 2 Type II certification. Make sure proper authorization forms are executed, maintain secure document storage, and implement access controls limiting who can view sensitive records.
